title: Calendar Days With Zero Orders
description:
Considering the full range from the earliest to the latest `order_date` in `orders`, report every calendar date **in that range** on which no order was placed at all.

Name the column `missing_date`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
WITH RECURSIVE spine(d) AS (
  SELECT MIN(order_date) FROM orders
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(d, '+1 day') FROM spine WHERE d < (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM orders)
)
SELECT d AS missing_date
FROM spine
WHERE d IS NOT NULL
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.order_date = d);
hint: There's no table of "all possible dates" to join against, so build one: a recursive CTE that starts at the earliest date and adds one day at a time up to the latest. Guard against an empty orders table, where MIN/MAX are both NULL.
outputExplanation: Only 6 dates between January 10, 2022 and January 2, 2023 have orders. Every other calendar day in that range — over 300 dates — had no orders and is reported.
